column2: The gates of [great_sack_province.GetName] lie in splinters and my warriors pour through them, howling the names of the Dark Gods. The great city that has stood for centuries is ours to do with as we please. Its temples will be pulled down, its people put in chains or to the sword, and its treasure is heaped before me. The gods are watching. What will I give them?

WAAAGH! The walls of [great_sack_province.GetName] are down, and the boyz are running through the streets smashing everything that stands still and stomping everything that runs. There is loot for the taking, shiny stuff in every house and plenty of humies to krump. The big city is ours!

The walls of [great_sack_province.GetName] have fallen and the herd floods into the city of men, braying and bellowing. Gors smash down the doors, ungors drag the screaming townsfolk from their hiding places, and bestigors topple the statues of the man-gods. The works of civilisation lie open to our horns. Let it all return to the wild!

[great_sack_province.GetName] has fallen. The great city that thought its walls would keep out the riders of the steppe has learned otherwise. My warriors ride through its streets driving herds of captives and wagons heaped with silk, silver and grain. A city like this has not been taken in a generation!
Strip it of everything of value!

Terrible news: [great_sack_province.GetName] has fallen to [From.GetTitledName] and the hordes of the Dark Gods. Refugees say the temples burn, the streets run with blood, and the Chaos warriors raise skull-cairns in the market squares. The great city may never be what it was.

Terrible news: [great_sack_province.GetName] has fallen to the greenskin Waaagh of [From.GetTitledName]. The orcs and goblins are tearing the city apart for loot and sport, and the few who escaped speak of horrors best left untold. The great city may never be what it was.

Terrible news: [great_sack_province.GetName] has fallen to [From.GetTitledName] and the beast-herds of the forest. The Children of Chaos are smashing everything that men have built, and the survivors speak of a herdstone raised before the great temple. The great city may never be what it was.

Terrible news: [great_sack_province.GetName] has fallen to [From.GetTitledName] and the riders of the steppe. They are driving off its people as slaves and its wealth in wagons, and what they cannot carry they burn. The great city may never be what it was.
This shame will not be forgotten!
May the gods have mercy on its people.
A horde sacked this great city. Its markets are ash, its people scattered or in chains, and it will take years to rise again.
